text:
marco: heads up — noticed a weird pattern on eu-west GPUs this morning. a few tenants in shared pools are causing long tail latencies, dedicated pools not getting filled as fallback. anyone else seeing 'alloc sandwich' bursts?
tara: yup, saw it ~08:12UTC. tail spikes ~3-5s for short seq jobs. looks like fabric congestion + sudden kv-cache churn.
olivia: I have a trace, there's a tiny window where requests route to hot host then bounce. probably NIC queue takeover.
kevin: can you paste the trace? also: are these preemptible or reserved?
marco: they're mostly preemptible starters (burst jobs). short-lived but high-concurrency. trace: 
```
reqID=abc123 route=shared-pool-eu-west host=eu-w-12 nic_q=96 cpu=48 gpu=1 rt=3.9s -> spill to eu-w-07 -> rt=6.2s
```
tara: interesting — eu-w-12 shows high PCIe utilization. I saw pcie resets on that rack recently.
marco: cost angle: these short bursts are cheap per-job but amplify tail latency and increase retries; net cost up.
oncall-erin: I'll run a quick probe to mark noisy hosts. putting a soft-deny for hosts with >80% pcie for 10m.
infra-bot: probe started: probe-id=probe-1714509999 targets=eu-w-12,eu-w-07 window=10m
kevin: also recommend enabling hard fallback to reserved-dedicated for jobs tagged critical=true for the next 30m. config snippet I suggest: 
```
routing.policy:
  prefer: shared
  overflow:
    - target: dedicated:eu-west
      when: pcie_util>75 or nic_drop>0.5
      ttl: 30m
```
olivia: that looks reasonable. but watchdedicated capacity — we only have 20% headroom in eu-west. if too many overflow we'll start evictions.
tara: can we instead do lightweight KV prefetching and small batching to smooth the burst? reduces KV churn.
marco: good call. can we flip prefetch=on for bursty tenant label 'burst-v1' for 20m and monitor?
oncall-erin: doing it now. toggled prefetch for label=burst-v1 -> true; will revert after 20m.
infra-bot: toggle acknowledged: prefetch=on label=burst-v1 expires=1714512076
kevin: I'll open a short runbook for manual evict+fallback if tail >5s for 5m. link: https://internal/runbooks/alloc-sandwich
marco: after 10m of the probe, eu-w-12 still shows queue pressure but tail reduced to ~1.6-2.1s. seems prefetch helped.
olivia: confirm. patch looks promising. next steps: 1) add an autoscaler override for dedicated pools during burst windows; 2) schedule a rack-level NIC firmware check for eu-w-12; 3) revisit allocation policy to prefer cold-start spread.
tara: +1. I'll draft the autoscaler override PR.
marco: thanks. summary: prefetch toggle + soft-deny on saturated hosts + TTLed overflow to dedicated = keeps service while we fix hardware. if anything regresses ping @oncall-erin. :thumbsup:
